questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Angle Modulation (Frequency Modulation: FM & Phase Modulation: PM)
questions.text: Derive the mathematical expression for Amplitude Modulated (DSB-FC) wave: $s(t) = A_c [1 + m(t)] \cos(2\pi f_c t)$. Derive the total transmitted power $P_t = P_c \left(1 + \frac{\mu^2}{2}\right)$ and modulation efficiency $\eta = \frac{\mu^2}{2 + \mu^2}$. Calculate total power for $100\%$ modulation ($\mu = 1$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Angle Modulation (Frequency Modulation: FM & Phase Modulation: PM)
questions.text: Compare DSB-SC, SSB-SC, and VSB modulation in terms of bandwidth, transmission power efficiency, and demodulator complexity. Explain the generation of SSB-SC using Phase Discrimination (Hartley method) and Frequency Discrimination (Filter method).

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to Communication Systems & Signal Transmission
questions.text: Derive the frequency spectrum of Frequency Modulated (FM) wave using Bessel functions: $s(t) = A_c \sum_{n=-\infty}^\infty J_n(\beta) \cos[2\pi (f_c + n f_m)t]$. State Carson's Rule for transmission bandwidth: $B_T = 2(\Delta f + f_m) = 2 f_m(1 + \beta)$. Compare Narrowband FM (NBFM) vs Wideband FM (WBFM).

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Angle Modulation (Frequency Modulation: FM & Phase Modulation: PM)
questions.text: Explain Pulse Code Modulation (PCM): Sampling, Quantization, and Encoding. Derive the Signal-to-Quantization Noise Ratio for a full-scale sinusoidal signal: $(SNR)_{dB} = 6.02 n + 1.76\,\text{dB}$ where $n$ is the number of bits per sample. Explain Companding (A-law and $\mu$-law companders).

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Angle Modulation (Frequency Modulation: FM & Phase Modulation: PM)
questions.text: Explain Delta Modulation (DM) and Adaptive Delta Modulation (ADM). Explain Slope Overload Distortion and Granular Noise in DM and derive the condition to prevent slope overload: $A_m \le \frac{\Delta}{2\pi f_m T_s}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Angle Modulation (Frequency Modulation: FM & Phase Modulation: PM)
questions.text: Explain Quadrature Phase Shift Keying (QPSK) and Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (16-QAM, 32-QAM). Draw the QPSK transmitter block diagram, receiver block diagram, and signal space constellation diagram. Derive the bit error probability $P_b = Q\left(\sqrt{\frac{2E_b}{N_0}}\right)$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to Communication Systems & Signal Transmission
questions.text: Represent the binary sequence $11010010$ in Line Coding formats: (a) Unipolar NRZ, (b) Polar NRZ, (c) Bipolar AMI (Alternate Mark Inversion), (d) Manchester, and (e) Differential Manchester encoding. Compare their power spectra and clock recovery capability.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to Communication Systems & Signal Transmission
questions.text: Define Information, Entropy ($H(X) = -\sum p_i \log_2 p_i$), Mutual Information, and Channel Capacity. State Shannon-Hartley Theorem: $C = B \log_2\left(1 + \frac{S}{N}\right)$. A telephone channel has bandwidth $3.4\,\text{kHz}$ and $SNR = 30\,\text{dB}$. Calculate the theoretical channel capacity.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to Communication Systems & Signal Transmission
questions.text: Explain Shannon-Fano Coding and Huffman Source Coding algorithm. A discrete memoryless source emits 5 symbols with probabilities $p(s_1) = 0.4, p(s_2) = 0.2, p(s_3) = 0.2, p(s_4) = 0.1, p(s_5) = 0.1$. Construct the binary Huffman code, calculate average code word length $L$, entropy $H(S)$, and coding efficiency $\eta = \frac{H(S)}{L}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Noise in Analog Communication Systems & SNR Analysis
questions.text: Explain Time Division Multiplexing (TDM - E1 and T1 carrier framing) and Frequency Division Multiplexing (FDM). Explain Satellite Communication: Link Budget Analysis, Earth Station, Geostationary Orbit, Uplink/Downlink frequencies, and Transponder architecture.
